content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-maths-multiplication-by-zero","title":"Multiplication by Zero","quick":"Any number multiplied by zero is always zero. No matter how big the number is, zero groups of it means nothing at all.","full":"Multiplication means adding a number a certain number of times. If a kirana shop keeper has 31 rupees worth of candy in one basket, and you ask for 0 baskets, you get nothing, so you have 0 rupees worth of candy. That is 31 × 0 = 0. The '31' tells how much is in one group, but '0' tells how many groups we are taking. Zero groups means nothing exists, no matter how big the group was. So for this question, 31 × 0 = 0.","tip":"Zero groups of anything means nothing: number × 0 is always 0.","answer":"0","traps":["Writing 31 as the answer instead of 0","Confusing 31×0 with 31×1 which gives 31","Thinking a big number times zero should give something big"],"misconception":"Child thinks a big number multiplied by zero should still give a big answer because the number itself is large.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If you have 5 empty boxes and each box has 0 apples, how many apples do you have?","expected_answer_hint":"0 apples, since there is nothing in each box"},{"q":"What is 100 × 0?","expected_answer_hint":"0, because any number times zero is zero"}],"check_question":{"q":"45 × 0 = ____","options":["0","45","1"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct!
